courses.name: A1 Grammar: Discover Daily Routines with Le Hoang Nam
courses.description: Guided discovery practice for present simple routines, third-person endings, negatives, and questions.

topics.name: Notice the Routine Pattern
topics.description: Notice present simple affirmative patterns in daily schedules.

lessons.title: Daily Routines and Third-Person Endings
lessons.description: Use daily schedules to notice when a verb takes s or es.
lessons.content: Look at the pattern before naming the rule: I walk to school, but Maya walks to school. He watches TV after dinner. With he, she, or it, most present simple verbs take -s; verbs such as watch take -es.

questions.questionText: Mina ___ breakfast at seven every morning.
questions.explanation: Mina is one person, so the present simple verb takes -s: Mina eats breakfast.

questions.questionText: Choose the sentence that matches Leo's schedule.
questions.explanation: Leo is he, so the verb go takes -es: Leo goes to work at eight.
questions.correctAnswer: Leo goes to work at eight.
questions.knowledgePoint: goes with he, she, or it

options.text: Leo goes to work at eight.
Leo go to work at eight.
Leo going to work at eight.
Leo gos to work at eight.

questions.questionText: On her timetable, Sara ___ the bus at seven.
questions.explanation: Sara is one person, so catch changes to catches in the present simple.
questions.knowledgePoint: es after verbs ending in ch

questions.questionText: Which sentence is correct for one student named Tom?
questions.explanation: For he, she, or it, read becomes reads in the present simple.
questions.correctAnswer: Tom reads a book at night.
questions.knowledgePoint: s with regular present simple verbs

options.text: Tom reads a book at night.
Tom read a book at night.
Tom reading a book at night.
Tom reades a book at night.

questions.questionText: The schedule says: We ___ English on Monday.
questions.explanation: We is more than one person, so the base verb study is used without -s.

topics.name: Ask About the Schedule
topics.description: Build present simple negatives and questions with do and does.

lessons.title: Do and Does in Daily Questions
lessons.description: Complete simple negative and question task cards about routines.
lessons.content: Notice the helper first: Does Ana play tennis? No, she does not play tennis. After does or does not, use the base verb play, not plays. Use do with I, you, we, and they.

questions.questionText: Task card: Ben does not ___ coffee in the morning.
questions.explanation: After does not, use the base verb drink: Ben does not drink coffee.

questions.questionText: Task card: ___ your parents work on Saturday?
questions.explanation: Your parents means they, so use do to begin the present simple question.

questions.questionText: Choose the question for one person, Emma.
questions.explanation: Emma is she, so use does, followed by the base verb like.

questions.questionText: Task card: I ___ not watch TV before school.
questions.explanation: With I, use do not and the base verb watch.

questions.questionText: A schedule asks about one child: What ___ Noah do after lunch?
questions.explanation: Noah is one person, so use does; the main verb stays in the base form do.

courses.name: A1 Grammar: My Family and Things with Doan Thu Trang
courses.description: Task-card practice for possessive adjectives and affirmative have and has with familiar family items.

topics.name: Family Task Cards
topics.description: Match my, your, his, and her with familiar singular people and things.

lessons.title: Whose Bag Is It?
lessons.description: Complete short family task cards with the correct possessive adjective.
lessons.content: Use my for the speaker, your for the listener, his for one male person, and her for one female person. The possessive adjective comes before the singular noun: her book, his bike.

questions.questionText: Task card: I am Mai. This is ___ pencil.
questions.explanation: Mai is speaking about a pencil that belongs to Mai, so use my.

questions.questionText: You show Nam a phone. Say: Is this ___ phone?
questions.explanation: The phone belongs to the listener, so use your.

questions.questionText: This is Minh. The blue bike belongs to Minh. It is ___ bike.
questions.explanation: Minh is one male person, so use his before bike.
questions.knowledgePoint: his for a male person's possession

questions.questionText: Lan has a red hat. Point to it: It is ___ hat.
questions.explanation: Lan is one female person, so use her before hat.
questions.knowledgePoint: her for a female person's possession

questions.questionText: A card shows your sister and a book. Choose the sentence.
questions.explanation: The book belongs to your sister, so her comes before book.

topics.name: What Does the Family Have?
topics.description: Use have and has to describe family members and familiar possessions.

lessons.title: Family Possession Cards
lessons.description: Complete affirmative task cards with have or has.
lessons.content: Use has with he, she, and one person. Use have with I, you, we, and they. Look at the person on the card before choosing: My brother has a kite, but we have a ball.

questions.questionText: My brother ___ a small kite.
questions.explanation: My brother is one person, so use has.

questions.questionText: We ___ two pictures of our family.
questions.explanation: We uses the base form have, even when the possession is more than one item.

questions.questionText: Task card: Hoa ___ a new school bag.
questions.explanation: Hoa is one person, so the affirmative form is has.

questions.questionText: You and your sister ___ a red ball.
questions.explanation: You and your sister means two people, so use have.

questions.questionText: The card shows Dad. Choose the complete sentence.
questions.explanation: Dad is one person, so use has: Dad has a camera.
questions.knowledgePoint: has in an affirmative family sentence
